differences.judge_quote: Prior centring work in this project (`notes/synthesis.md`) shows that subtracting the family mean (`J_l (h - mu)`) dramatically improves the readout (association val cos 0.41 to 0.75 on 27B), because `mu` decodes to the continuation prior that dominates the uncentred top-10.
differences.what: contribution.md attributes the centring idea to a prior note in the project (notes/synthesis.md) and gives its 27B result; the user's message never mentions this prior work exists at all, presenting the centring-direction approach without any named antecedent.

differences.judge_quote: We replicate this centring effect through the forward pass.
differences.what: contribution.md explicitly frames the current method as a replication of an existing (prior) effect; the message instead describes it in its own voice as a method that 'approximates the centred J-lens readout', omitting the explicit 'replicate' framing and the implication that the core idea is not new.

differences.judge_quote: It differs from CAA (Panickssery et al. 2024) and ActAdd (Turner et al. 2023) in that the goal is readout quality rather than behavioural steering, and the contrast is between the association bench distribution and the null expansion point.
differences.what: contribution.md situates the method relative to two named prior steering papers (CAA, ActAdd); the message never names or discusses these related works.

differences.judge_quote: The herrera2026 negative result on generic attitude vectors for recall motivated focusing on the family-specific mean rather than a task-attitude direction.
differences.what: contribution.md credits a specific prior negative result (herrera2026) as motivating a design choice; the message gives no such attribution, instead listing the design exploration ('Other-family contrasts... all harmful') without crediting any prior work for motivating it.

rationale: contribution.md (seen by the judge) explicitly names and credits multiple prior sources — an in-project note (notes/synthesis.md) whose centring effect the method 'replicates', plus related published work (CAA, ActAdd) and a motivating negative result (herrera2026) — situating the contribution as a translation of existing findings into a new framework. The final message to the user describes the same method and numeric results but never names any of these sources or uses the word 'replicate', so the user receives a less complete picture of how much the work builds on pre-existing project knowledge and literature.
